flow-seam.blurb: one act leaves fast on an axis with motion blur, a frame of empty ground, the next act arrives on the same axis and direction while the ground changes colour

sources.note: editor window exits left, 'MADERA understands' enters from the right, word by word
tagline exits left word by word, product card enters from the right, ground darkens
card exits left over a red blurred-photo ground, ground fades to light grey, 'find' enters from the right
tagline exits up, ground turns olive, a tilted window rises from the bottom
window exits up, ground returns to light grey, a shape rises from the bottom

slots.at: seconds: the first frame of empty ground
slots.ground: [outgoing ground id, incoming ground id], optional

axis.note: x flows right to left, y flows bottom to top; madera changes axis once per film

gap.note: measured by make study as the core of empty-ground frames: 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.083 s across the five seams

stagger.note: words of an entering line lag each other. When the "in" layer already carries `split: "word"` (authored by a word-by-word line), the whole-layer slide this recipe would otherwise write is skipped and the words arrive on their own split track instead; this value then has no effect unless the word-by-word line's own `stagger` param is left at its default, which happens to be the same measured number

driftPx.note: small anticipation pull the wrong way before the rush

window-dolly.blurb: a slow continuous dolly-in that zooms the camera toward a named layer's box, tightening the frame across the whole shot with no cut

sources.note: act 1 (0s-4.54s): the agent window fills the frame steadily, the sidebar and prompt bar both growing larger frame to frame; boundary-pixel estimate off 3 sampled frames puts the push at roughly 1.9x by the cut
act 3 (6s-8.12s): a slight continuous push on the swipe-card stack, steady through each swipe; card-width estimate off 2 sampled frames puts it at roughly 1.25x, visibly gentler than act 1

act 5 (9.57s-11.08s): a slow dolly-in on the results window as its product grid fills in; sidebar-width estimate off 2 sampled frames puts it at roughly 1.15x, the shortest act of the three so the smallest push

slots.target: layer id: the layer the camera dollies toward (its box gives the point the camera centres on)

zoomTo.note: measured scale reached by push end: act 1 ~1.9 over 4.54s, act 3 ~1.25 over 2.12s, act 5 ~1.15 over 1.51s (boundary-pixel triangulation off sampled frames per act, moderate confidence, one source each). 1.3 is a rounded cross-act default; an author should usually override with a figure scaled to their own push's duration rather than trust the default blind

headroom.note: diveIn's own frame-fill cap, unchanged: the target may fill at most 88% of the canvas on either axis

ease.note: diveIn's own built-in feel (fast in, long settle); matches the measured deceleration into every madera push. Not yet measured to differ, so not offered as a real choice

word-by-word.blurb: a line arrives one word after another, each word rising into place, for a tagline or headline entrance instead of the whole line sliding in as one block

sources.note: act 2: 'MADERA understands your taste.' enters word by word from the right, each word landing in its own colour before the line settles to one ink
act 4: 'MADERA find items you love.' enters the same way

slots.layer: layer id: a text layer carrying the line
slots.colors: [hex, ...]? optional. One colour: routes through colorWave's `flash`. Two or more: routes through colorWave's `colors` (core/kinetic/presets.js), so word i arrives in colors[i % n] then eases to `settle`
slots.settle: colour or null? optional, only read when `colors` names 2+. Default: that layer's own ink, matching the measured film (each word lands in its own colour before the line settles to one ink). Pass null to keep every word its own colour forever instead
slots.exit: { preset, at, each?, stagger?, from?, ease? }? optional. Copied straight onto the layer's own `exit` (core/tracks/units.js): the line leaves word by word, `at` seconds after ITS OWN start, reusing the entrance preset vocabulary reversed. Left unconfigured, `each`/`stagger` default to 60% of this line's own arrival timing and `ease` to `easeInCubic`, so the exit reads faster and more decided than the entrance it mirrors, never a same-speed rewind

preset.note: core/kinetic/presets.js PRESETS.up: rise + fade per split unit, the engine's default kinetic reveal and the closest named match to madera's word-by-word rise

each.note: per-unit reveal duration; matches flow-seam's enterDur, the closest measured entrance timing in this film

stagger.note: per-word lag, measured off acts 2 and 4 the same way flow-seam's own stagger note was written before expand.mjs could split text: consecutive words visibly lag by 2 to 4 frames at 60fps

object-wipe.blurb: a full-bleed page slides across the frame on a hard edge while the next page is already visible underneath it the whole time, no empty ground and no gap, both scenes live at once, like swiping between two app screens

sources.note: a warm-toned browser page fills the frame, then a cool blue page enters from the right and slides fully across it: at 0.50s the swipe peaks (curve value 9.5, the loudest frame in the shot), by 1.25s the hard edge sits near mid-frame with both pages simultaneously visible either side of it, by 1.77s the blue page has fully taken over. The browser chrome stays fixed and only recolours to match whichever page currently fills the frame. No empty frame ever appears between the two: unlike flow-seam, there is no ground gap, the outgoing and incoming pages are directly adjacent at every instant

slots.out: layer id: the full-bleed page leaving
slots.in: layer id: the full-bleed page arriving

direction.note: arc-space-swiping's incoming page enters from the right edge and travels left, pushing the outgoing page off the left edge

dur.note: measured off the shot's own curve: it rises to its peak (9.5) at 0.50s into the 1.5s shot and has settled to near-zero (0.4, then 0) by 0.75-1.0s, so the visible swipe itself runs about half a second

ease.note: the curve decelerates into its landing rather than running linear; not independently timed frame by frame, so this is a convention default matching the shape, not a fitted curve

colour-wipe.blurb: a solid colour panel sweeps across the frame edge to edge in a hard fast wipe and becomes the next background, no fade, no empty frame, no gap, the panel's own colour IS the new ground rather than something removed once it arrives

sources.note: the engine's own seam detector measured a 4-frame (0.067s @60fps) axis-x, left-to-right ground change from #bababb (light) to #3e3e3e (dark) at this timestamp (grammar/make-it-move.json seams[2]); frames extracted at 20fps either side of it show a dark rectangle sweeping left to right across the visible 'slide it up' line, covering the frame in well under a tenth of a second and leaving the dark ground and the next line ('wooh!') already in place behind it. The panel is not seen to fade or shrink afterward: it simply is the new ground from that point on

slots.shape: layer id: a full-bleed solid-colour panel matching the incoming scene's ground colour
slots.out: layer id, optional: outgoing content to drop (opacity 0) once the panel has fully covered the frame, since the panel already occludes it visually and this only stops it rendering

sweepDur.note: the 4-frame @60fps gap the seam detector measured between groundBefore and groundAfter at make-it-move t=4.63

ease.note: not independently measurable at 4 frames' resolution; a convention default so the sweep does not read as a linear mechanical slide

hover-click.blurb: a cursor eases onto a named control's live box, switches to a hand, and clicks it: the one move every cursor demo in this library already makes by hand-typing pixels

sources.note: cursor arrives over the install button at 0.8s into its own path, clicks 0.15s later
same shape: arrives at 0.8s, clicks at 0.95s, 0.15s after arrival
arrives at 1.3s, clicks at 1.5s, 0.2s after arrival
arrives at 0.5s, clicks at 0.6629s, 0.163s after arrival

the vawe-type demo worked example: cursor and click land on 'save-btn' at the same instant, no gap. Not a filmed clip like the other sources here, this engine's own canonical demo, kept as a source because every number above still had to be typed as raw pixels by hand until this recipe existed

slots.at: seconds: when the cursor arrives on the target's box
slots.target: layer id: the control being clicked

edge.note: which point on the target's live box the cursor lands on (core/layers/cursor.js EDGES: center/above/below/left/right); center matches every measured source

approach.note: the snapTo ease-in window before arrival (core/layers/cursor.js resolveSnap default). Not a value measured off one clip: real approach distances range 0.8s to 5.5s across the sources above, so this keeps the engine's own default rather than fabricate one number for every layout

clickDelay.note: gap from arrival to click: measured 0.15s (brew-native, example-product-promo), 0.163s (vawe-flow-2), 0.2s (preface-launch), 0s (the worked demo). 0.15s is the plurality

style.note: the shape the cursor switches to for the approach, before the click: a hand reads as hovering something clickable (core/layers/cursor.js CURSOR_STYLES)

orbit-path.blurb: motionPath: a layer flies a real curved path instead of a straight motion-key tween, GSAP MotionPathPlugin driving position off an authored SVG curve

sources.note: not a filmed clip: quality/baselines/reach.json named motionPath a validated, GSAP-wired field with zero authored uses and no named capability pointing an author at it, so this engine's own probe is the source until a real film reaches for it

slots.at: seconds: when the layer starts its run
slots.path: an SVG path `d` string, in the layer's own local px

align.note: GSAP MotionPathPlugin `align`: "self" moves the layer's own box along the path

autoRotate.note: true turns the layer to face the path's own tangent as it travels

curviness.note: GSAP's smoothing of the control points between path keys; 1 is untouched

line-reveal.blurb: splitText: each LINE of a text layer masks and slides up from behind on its own stagger, GSAP SplitText at line granularity (char/word stay with the engine's own `split`)

sources.note: not a filmed clip: splitText was validated and GSAP-wired with zero authored uses, and its only near-hit in the docs was the unrelated internal `split` helper, a false friend for a search

slots.at: seconds: when the layer starts revealing
slots.layer: layer id: a multi-line text layer

dur.note: per-line reveal time (SplitText's own default, core/scene.js)

stagger.note: gap between one line's reveal starting and the next

mask.note: false drops the clip mask and fades the line in instead of sliding it up from behind one

scatter-burst.blurb: physics: a layer's own split characters fly apart under real velocity/gravity/friction, GSAP Physics2DPlugin giving each an index-based angle spread so the scatter is wide and deterministic, never a shared straight-line tween

sources.note: not a filmed clip: physics was validated and GSAP-wired, zero authored uses, the plan's own confirmed unreachable example

slots.at: seconds: when the layer starts scattering

angle.note: the centre launch angle, -90 is straight up; each split unit spreads around it

gravity.note: px/s^2 pulling the scatter back down

friction.note: 0-1, air drag on the launch velocity

spread.note: total angle the split units fan across, centred on `angle`

time-ramp.blurb: timeRemap: a layer's own clock warps under a named shape (whip/hold/freeze/rewind), so everything it does, motion, count, idle, speeds and slows together instead of one property being eased alone

sources.note: core/timeline/time.js's SHAPES already carry real measured uses under their own names (`whip` alone: core/timeline/time.js catalog); the gap this recipe closes is that `timeRemap`, the field name itself, answered no search for it, only its shape names did

slots.at: seconds: when the layer starts (also its motion track's own clock)

shape.note: core/timeline/time.js TIME_REMAP_REGISTRY names; each is a catalogued, measured clock curve, not an invented one
